Data & methodology

Behind the forecast.

What the numbers mean, and how to read them.

01 / DATA

A synthetic market replay

Every stock has 90 generated weekday closing prices ending 6 November 2026. They are seeded fixtures, not exchange quotes. Event probabilities and volumes are separate synthetic fixtures.

No live API, trading service, or AI model is connected.

02 / FORECAST

A trailing trend baseline

The next close is estimated from the latest six closes: last close plus 55% of the average daily change across that window. The same slope extends over five future weekday sessions.

next = last + 0.55 × (last − sixth) / 5
03 / BACKTEST

Error measured before the result

For each of the final 30 sessions, a one-step forecast uses only earlier closes. MAE is the average absolute dollar error. MAPE is the average absolute error divided by the observed price.

Directional accuracy counts forecasts on the correct side of the preceding close. Flat observed sessions are excluded.

04 / UNCERTAINTY

A range, with limits

The band is the median ± 1.645 × backtest RMSE × √horizon, clamped above zero. “90%” assumes normal independent residuals; coverage is not validated and can be lower.

Metrics describe synthetic history only. They do not establish performance on real markets. Forecast direction and event prices are independent.

Inspect the data

Export every stock’s closing prices, one-step backtest predictions, and five-session forecasts as a CSV file.

Paper orders use whole shares and cent-based accounting. Cash and trades stay in local browser storage. There are no fees or settlements.
